decisions.note: English has a typo: "How should I eat ths?". Source text, so it cannot be corrected.
「お話し中すみません」 is "sorry to interrupt", not "May I cut in?".
"By this point today is that child also a highschool student?" is not grammatical English.
"A woman is going into it now" — "it" has no antecedent when the sentence stands alone.
An English proverb substituted for a Japanese one; it translates nothing in the source.
Fragment. Loses the question — "is Galileo Galilei his real name?".
JP states that they will be able to meet from time to time; EN turns it into an invitation.
午後 is the afternoon, not the evening — the translation contradicts the meaning 午 is teaching.
Proverb substituted, and its number differs from the 七十五 the sentence is demonstrating.
"The idea made my soul rise" is not idiomatic English.
Dangling relative clause; "who was outside" attaches to the balcony and reverses who is where.
通り雨 is a passing shower, not a tropical storm.
"above London" for 北 teaches the wrong English word for the kanji being learned.
"lies just above London" for 北 — same defect as its sibling sentence.
"This is five thousand yen in the Japanese Yen" is ungrammatical and tautological. Both sides flagged non-native.
An English proverb substituted for a Japanese one; it translates nothing, and 百 = hundred survives nowhere in the English.
Proverb substituted rather than translated, and the sentence is above-N1 (枯 is never taught).
"for a rainy day" is an English idiom swapped in for 万一 ("in case of emergency"); teaches nothing of 万 = ten thousand.
English invents "the porch door", absent from the Japanese, and reverses the direction: the cat entered the veranda, it did not come in from it. Rank 1 for 入.
Subject mismatch: 「日本に来てから十年になります」 is first person, rendered "since he came to Japan". tatoeba-122378-281625 renders the identical construction correctly with "I". Rank 1 for 十.
"rainshower" is not a word — "rain shower" or "shower". Same class of source typo as the 食 "ths" rejection.
西洋人 is "Westerner", not "European". The mistranslation lands directly on the sense of 西 this slot is teaching.
Dangling "it" with no antecedent, and a meaning inversion: 白日の下に晒される is exposure to public scrutiny, whereas "see the light of day" is being finally realised.
Typo in the JAPANESE source: 「電話をかけなくてははらない」 should be ならない. Verbatim licensed text, so it cannot be corrected.
「約半リットル」 rendered "one pint": drops 半 — the target kanji — and silently changes the unit.
古今東西 rendered "a universal truth that transcends time": 東西 is dropped entirely, so the target kanji has no counterpart in the English.
「トムは高校時代の友人です」 rendered "Tom and I went to the same high school" — 友人 is dropped and the English asserts something the Japanese does not.
「楽しく読めます」 rendered "This book will give you great pleasure" — the target kanji 読 has no counterpart in the English.
「あのレースは八百長だった」 / "The race was fixed". 八百長 is fixing a match; neither 八 nor 百 nor 長 has a counterpart in the English. Held three publishing slots at once — 八#2, 百#2, 長#3.

「このゲームは八百長だ」 / "This game is fixed". The same idiom as tatoeba-231233-68601 and rejected for the same reason. It sits at 八#8 and 百#6 today rather than in a publishing slot, but keeping one 八百長 while rejecting the other would be incoherent, and a regenerated queue can promote it.
「十中八九ジェーンは来るだろう」 / "It is probable that Jane will come". 十中八九 is "in all likelihood"; the English carries none of the three numerals. Held 九#2 and 十#3.
「トムが四六時中電話してくるの」 / "Tom calls me all the time". 四六時中 is "around the clock" (4 × 6 = 24); "all the time" contains neither number. Held 四#2 and 六#2.

The second 四六時中 sentence, "…only thinks about work all the time". Same idiom and same ruling as tatoeba-9250570-3405512; at 六#8 today, but rejected with its sibling so a regeneration cannot promote it into a publishing slot.
「時間なんて山ほどあった」 / "We had plenty of time". 山ほど is a quantity idiom — the English says "plenty", never "mountain". Rank 1 for 山, so this is the most expensive entry in the class.
「トムはレタスを千切りにした」 / "Tom shredded the lettuce". 千切り is julienne; the thousand is figurative and absent from the English. Rank 3 for 千.
「車のバッテリーが上がってるよ」 / "My car battery is dead". バッテリーが上がる is a battery going flat — the one sense of 上 in which nothing goes up. Rank 2 for 上.

「何とおっしゃいましたか」 / "I beg your pardon?". 何 is doing its ordinary "what" job in the Japanese, but the idiomatic English paraphrases it away entirely, so the pair teaches the reader nothing about the character. Rank 3 for 何.
